audit.whatIsWrong: Six separate fields describe Supreme Display of Talent as a 'flash-dash' that lets Qiyana jump onto you and reset the fight: spikes[1].text, whys[4], mid, late, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Riot's text: Qiyana sends out a shockwave that detonates whatever elements she hits with it, stunning and damaging nearby enemies — 950 range, 120s flat, projectile, knockup/hardCC, terrain. It has no dash component at all. Her gap-closers are Audacity (E, 650 range, 11/10/9/8/7s) and Terrashape (W, 1100 range dash, 7s). A player told to hold the stun 'for when she flash-dashes in' with her ultimate will hold it forever.
audit.corrected: The ultimate is a terrain-detonating stun shockwave; the dash that reaches you is Audacity, and Terrashape is how she re-enters.
sources: brief enemyKit Q/W/E/R text, ranges and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with itself in two directions: phases[].side vs win[] on four rows, and within the content layer win[4]/win[5] are the reverse of what whys[4]/whys[5] and spikes[1]/spikes[2] say.
audit.why: whys[4] says level 6 favours Qiyana (her ultimate) and whys[5] says first item favours Annie (Luden's burst). That is the correct reading of both kits: Qiyana's 120s ultimate is her only lane-defining spike, and Annie's first item is hers. win[] currently has those two rows swapped.
audit.corrected: Chart should read Annie, Skill, Skill, Annie, Qiyana, Annie, Annie across both layers.

audit.corrected: Even-to-favoured; the only losing picture is an unstacked Annie inside 650 with Audacity up.

notes: The dominant defect here is not a wrong name but a wrong mechanic repeated six times: Supreme Display of Talent was written as a flash-dash gap-closer. It is a 950-range shockwave that detonates terrain and stuns; her gap-closers are Audacity (E) and Terrashape (W). Also removed 'one-shots Qiyana from stealth' in `late` — Annie has no stealth. Level chart: the content layer contradicted itself — win[4]=Annie/win[5]=Qiyana while whys[4] gives level 6 to Qiyana and whys[5] gives first item to Annie. I judged the whys correct (her only lane spike is the 120s ultimate; Annie's is Luden's) and proposed the whole chart as one group across both layers, which means win[4] and win[5] swap and phases[4]/[5].why were rewritten to match. This deliberately departs from packet.levelChart on those two rows — flagged for the user.
